firstText: Keep a backup of important files. Read the audit and its limitations, then ask about any proposal you do not understand. Approve exact codes only after reviewing the plan.
safetyTitle: Control is part of the design.
safetyIntro: The report informs your decision. It never grants permission to change files.
safetyReview: A fixed plan, explicit file IDs and a digest bind the supported operation.
safetyRecovery: Quarantine needs intact files and journals. Purge cannot be undone. Neither replaces your backup.
safetySystem: Tuning, repair and uninstall remain advice until a tested procedure exists. Untested environments stay unverified.
safetyPrivacy: Reports can contain paths and machine details. Review an aggregate export before sharing; your agent provider has its own data boundary.
learnTitle: A little context goes a long way.
faqSpaceTitle: Why not delete every large folder?
faqSpace: A large folder may hold projects, application data or virtual disks. Measured size is evidence to review, not a promise of reclaimable space.
faqSpeedTitle: Will cleanup make my PC faster?
faqSpeed: It depends on the bottleneck. Freeing storage does not remove CPU work from a running application. Syrin clean keeps performance advice separate from file cleanup.
faqOfflineTitle: Can I use this HTML offline?
faqOffline: Yes. Fonts, the sample report, both packages and prompt generation are embedded. Your agent or package installers may still need a network connection for their own work.
faqSupportTitle: Which machines and agents are verified?
faqSupport: The support matrix separates implemented behavior from tested environments. A passing fixture test does not qualify every Windows version, device, filesystem or agent.
